decision.detail: I walk past the ballroom door without stopping. The lights are warm and the crowd is murmuring and someone's laughing, and I don't turn my head. I go to the station line. The patch window is open. I set the reel on the counter. It's small. It's the one I'm allowed to ship. I tap it once with my knuckle so the tag is facing up, the way you'd set a can of film on a shelf. The operator on the other side nods. I don't wait for a receipt. I pull my coat collar up. The last train window is on the wall. I check it. Thursday's not the only one. There's one Tuesday night, nine-forty, if the line runs clean. I'll be on it. I don't look back at the ballroom. I don't say anything to the operator. I just set the reel down, step back, and walk to the platform.
decision.intention: Get the reel onto the regional line tonight. Pittsburgh by Thursday at the latest. The shot is done. The job is the reel in the hand of someone who can move it. After that I'm a man with an empty bag and a train to catch.

messages.content: You are Larry, the camera operator. You've got one charged recording. The lights at the festival look spectacular; an old projectionist also wants to say a few words. You decide what to shoot and what to do after work. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
